Tatistcheff
Receives Two
Months' Term

Count Vladimir Tatistcheff, 40-
year-old Russian emigre, was sen-
tenced to two months' imprisonment
in the First Special District Court
yesterday morning, after being
found guilty on a charge of de-
frauding another Russian of $8,000
in a cigarette deal.

The accused Russian, who has
several previous convictions both in
the Settlement and Concession, re-
ceived a deposit of $8,000 from Mr.
I. S. Raskin after promising to de-
liver 1,000 tins of Camel cigarettes.

Testimony in court revealed that
Tatistcheff approached the Russian
broker and asked him to find a
buyer for 2,000 tins of Camel
cigarettes, which the former said he
could obtain at $55 per tin. It was
agreed that they would sell the
cigarettes at $85 per tin, with the
profits being split evenly.

Raskin then contacted a Portu-
guese broker named Carlos A. da
Conceicao, who agreed to purchase
1,000 tins of the cigarettes, at the
price set by Tatistcheff. After
agreeing on the deal at the Palace
Hotel, the accused demanded a de-
posit of $8,000 with the promise
that the cigarettes would be deliver-
ed to 24 Central Arcade later on the
same day.

The Portuguese broker was given
a written guarantee by Mr. Raskin,
promising to refund the advance on
demand, and after Tatistcheff failed
to deliver the cargo, the complainant
informed the police. Tatistcheff was
apprehended on Avenue Joffre 24
hours later, with the assistance of
the French Police, and admitted the
fraud.

(S.E.)
DATE 8/3 43

塔季谢夫
获刑两个月

弗拉基米尔·塔季谢夫伯爵（Count Vladimir Tatistcheff），40岁，俄国流亡者，昨日上午在第一特区地方法院被判处两个月监禁，罪名是欺诈另一名俄国人8,000美元香烟交易款。

该被告俄国人此前在租界和法租界均有数次定罪记录，他在承诺交付1,000听骆驼牌（Camel）香烟后，从I. S. Raskin先生处收取了8,000美元定金。

法庭证词显示，塔季谢夫接触这位俄国经纪人，请他为其寻找买家，出售2,000听骆驼牌香烟，并称其能以每听55美元的价格获得货源。双方商定以每听85美元的价格出售香烟，利润平分。

随后，Raskin联系了一位名为Carlos A. da Conceicao的葡萄牙经纪人，对方同意按塔季谢夫设定的价格购买1,000听香烟。在皇宫饭店（Palace Hotel）谈妥交易后，被告要求支付8,000美元定金，并承诺香烟将于当天晚些时候送至中央商场（Central Arcade）24号。

Raskin先生向这位葡萄牙经纪人出具了一份书面担保，承诺按需退还预付款。由于塔季谢夫未能交付货物，投诉人向警方报案。24小时后，在法国警察的协助下，塔季谢夫在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）被捕，并承认了诈骗行为。

(S.E.)
日期 1943年8月3日

档案：V. Tatistcheff

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JUNE 12, 1936

“Count” Tatisheff Sentenced
** ** ** ** ** **
Convicted Of Pawning Typewriter

Vladimir Tatisheff, who claims the title of Count Tatisheff, was sentenced to two months' imprisonment by the First Special District Court yesterday morning after he had been convicted of pawning a typewriter which he had borrowed from Mr. E. Marques at the Candy Shop in the Central Arcade. The deed was said to have been committed on June 2.

Tatisheff, although charged with a minor offense, managed to gain an important spot in the news when he appeared in the Italian Consular Court two days ago and testified that V. Pinto had confessed to him of burgling his own bank last September. Tatisheff and Pinto were cell-mates at the Central Police Station.

When sentence was pronounced yesterday morning, the Count asked for leniency on the grounds that this was his first offense. He requested a suspended sentence but this, the court denied.

Tatisheff arrived in Shanghai about one year ago, coming from Spain. He speaks 12 languages and during most of his stay here, operated as a broker.

《字林西报》，1936年6月12日，星期五

“塔季谢夫伯爵”被判刑
** ** ** ** ** **
因典当打字机被判有罪

自称拥有塔季谢夫伯爵头衔的弗拉基米尔·塔季谢夫（Vladimir Tatisheff），昨日上午被第一特区地方法院判处两个月监禁，罪名是他将从E. Marques先生处借来的一台打字机在中央商场的糖果店（Candy Shop）典当。据称该行为发生于6月2日。

尽管塔季谢夫被控犯有轻罪，但他两天前出现在意大利领事法院，作证称V. Pinto向他承认去年九月盗窃了自己的银行，从而占据了新闻的重要版面。塔季谢夫和Pinto曾是中央捕房的同牢囚犯。

昨日上午宣判时，伯爵以初犯为由请求从轻发落。他请求缓刑，但被法庭驳回。

塔季谢夫约一年前从西班牙抵达上海。他会说12种语言，在此期间大部分时间从事经纪人工作。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JUNE 5, 1936

Russian Held
In Typewriter
Fraud Episode

Admits Pawning Machine
Loaned To Carry On
Literary Work

Blaming hard times and financial difficulty for his misadventure, Vladimir Tatisheff, 34-year-old Russian, brought up before the First Special District Court yesterday on charge of obtaining a $220 Underwood typewriter by fraud, asked the judge to be lenient because it was his first offense.

Tatisheff, according to the prosecution, borrowed the machine from a Portuguese, Mr. E. J. Marques, on the pretense what he wanted to type "some very important memoranda." The typewriter was later discovered by police at the Sung Kong Pawnshop, Woosung Road, where the accused had received $52.50 for the machine.

The acquaintance between the accused and Mr. Marques started in December last year. About three weeks ago, Tatisheff allegedly told Mr. Marques that he was planning to publish a weekly magazine. The two then went to 149 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, where the accused showed his friend the suite of offices which he claimed to have rented for his journalistic enterprise.

Knowing that Mr. Marques was then unemployed, Tatisheff offered him a job at $150 a month. On Tuesday, the pair met at the Junior Golf Club, Hongkew Park, and Tatisheff told his Portuguese friend that he needed a typewriter to type an important memorandum. He asked Mr. Marques to have the typewriter delivered to the Candy Shop, Central Arcade. The understanding between the two was that the machine would be returned at 10 o'clock the same evening.

At the appointed time, the machine failed to arrive. The next morning, Mr. Marques went to the Candy Shop and found a chit addressed to him saying that the typewriter would be returned 10 p.m. Wednesday.

On Wednesday evening, Mr. Marques again went to the Central Arcade address but the machine was not there. Suspecting that he was being defrauded, he went to the Central Police Station to report the case. On the way, he met the accused, and the two went to the station to clear up matters.

Tatisheff, questioned by the police, admitted that he pawned the machine. He also admitted that he obtained another typewriter, which he pawned, from 660 Szechuen Road.

Questioned by the judge yesterday, Tatisheff told the Court that the two cases of fraud were the only times he ever broke the law. He asked the court to consider a suspended sentence if he is found guilty.

Tatisheff's case was adjourned for a week pending further investigation of the other typewriter which the accused admitted taking.

《字林西报》，1936年6月5日，星期五

俄国人因打字机
诈骗案被捕

承认典当了
借来进行文学创作
的机器

34岁的俄国人弗拉基米尔·塔季谢夫（Vladimir Tatisheff）昨日因诈骗获取一台价值220美元的安德伍德（Underwood）打字机而被提审至第一特区地方法院。他将此次不幸归咎于时世艰难和经济困难，并以初犯为由请求法官从轻发落。

据检方指控，塔季谢夫从葡萄牙人E. J. Marques先生处借得该机器，借口是他需要打印“一些非常重要的备忘录”。警方后来在吴淞路的宋公当铺（Sung Kong Pawnshop）发现了这台打字机，被告以此获得了52.50美元。

被告与Marques先生的相识始于去年十二月。大约三周前，塔季谢夫据称告诉Marques先生，他计划出版一份周刊。随后两人前往圆明园路149号，被告向朋友展示了他声称为其新闻事业租下的办公室套房。

得知Marques先生当时失业，塔季谢夫以月薪150美元向他提供了一份工作。周二，两人在虹口公园的青年高尔夫俱乐部（Junior Golf Club）会面，塔季谢夫告诉他的葡萄牙朋友，他需要一台打字机来打印一份重要备忘录。他请Marques先生将打字机送到中央商场的糖果店。双方的约定是机器将于当晚10点归还。

到了约定时间，机器并未送达。次日早晨，Marques先生前往糖果店，发现一张写给他的便条，称打字机将于周三晚上10点归还。

周三晚上，Marques先生再次前往中央商场的地址，但机器不在那里。怀疑自己被骗后，他前往中央捕房报案。途中，他遇到了被告，两人一同前往捕房澄清事实。

经警方讯问，塔季谢夫承认典当了该机器。他还承认从四川北路660号获取了另一台打字机并将其典当。

昨日接受法官讯问时，塔季谢夫告诉法庭，这两起诈骗案是他唯一违法的经历。如果被判有罪，他请求法庭考虑缓刑。

鉴于需对被告承认拿走的另一台打字机进行进一步调查，塔季谢夫一案休庭一周。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date April 8, 1935.
Subject. Communication from American Consular Service Re: V.V. Tatischeff.
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by [Signature]

Count Vladimir Vladimirovitch Tatischeff arrived
in Shanghai from Naples on February 19, 1935, as a 3rd class
passenger on board the s.s. "Haruna Maru." From the Alien
Declaration Form filled in by him, it appears that he was born
in 1902 at St. Petersbourg, Russia, and that he is a "person
without nationality" under the protection of the Italian
Government (sic). He produced Russian passport No. 177 issued
on 28.1.1919 and renewed by the Italian Consul-General in
Barcelona. The passport bears a Chinese visa issued by the
Chinese Consulate in Venice on 6.9.34.

During the course of a conversation with members of
the Shanghai Municipal Police on board the s.s. "Haruna Maru,"
Tatischeff mentioned that he was a journalist by profession
and that he represented the "New York Herald." He also stated
that he intended to stay in Shanghai for some time and eventually
hoped to proceed to America, of which country he was anxious to
become a citizen. Enquiries made regarding Tatischeff on
board the ship show that in a casual conversation with one of
his fellow-passengers he had mentioned that he would make an
attempt to interest the Chinese in the purchase of arms of
Italian make.

Upon his arrival here, Tatischeff put up at No. 477
Rue Auguste Boppe, a Russian boarding house, where for the first
few days he shared a room with one Leo Berg, Swede, 46, who had
arrived in Shanghai together with him. A Russian female named
M.V. Danish, 33, who arrived from Marseilles in the same vessel,
also stayed at the above address. While the s.s. "Haruna Maru"
was in port, the trio visited the ship on several occasions
ostensibly for the purpose of seeing their friends.

主题. 美国领事事务处关于 V.V. Tatischeff 的来函。
撰写人 D.S. Tcheremshansky。 转发人 [签名]

弗拉基米尔·弗拉基米罗维奇·塔季谢夫伯爵（Count Vladimir Vladimirovitch Tatischeff）于1935年2月19日作为三等舱乘客，乘坐“春阳丸”号（s.s. "Haruna Maru"）轮船从那不勒斯抵达上海。从他填写的外侨登记表来看，他于1902年出生于俄国圣彼得堡，是一名受意大利政府保护的“无国籍人士”（原文如此）。他出示了1919年1月28日签发的俄国护照第177号，该护照由意大利驻巴塞罗那总领事续签。护照上贴有中国驻威尼斯领事馆于1934年9月6日签发的中国签证。

在“春阳丸”号轮船上与上海公共租界工部局警务处人员交谈期间，塔季谢夫提到他的职业是记者，代表《纽约先驱报》（New York Herald）。他还表示打算在上海停留一段时间，并最终希望前往美国，他渴望成为该国公民。在船上对塔季谢夫进行的调查显示，在与一名 fellow-passengers（同船乘客）的随意交谈中，他曾提及将尝试引起中国人对购买意大利制造武器的兴趣。

抵达上海后，塔季谢夫入住奥古斯特·博佩路（Rue Auguste Boppe）477号的一家俄国人寄宿公寓，起初几天他与一同抵达上海的46岁瑞典人Leo Berg共用一个房间。一位名叫M.V. Danish的33岁俄国女性也住在上述地址，她乘坐同一艘船从马赛抵达。在“春阳丸”号停靠港口期间，这三人曾多次登船， ostensibly（表面上）是为了看望朋友。

On February 20, 1935, the local Russian newspapers
published interviews with Count Tatischeff. It would appear
from these interviews that his father who was formerly Chairman
of the Union Bank in Moscow, following the outbreak of the
revolution in Russia left that country for Abyssinia, where he
subsequently died. At the age of 15 Tatischeff joined the
"White" Army. He saw active service during the civil war in
Russia, and was promoted to the rank of Lieutenant. Being
seriously wounded he was evacuated to Constantinople on board
an English ship. Later he resided at Malta and then in England,
where he studied law at the University of Oxford and obtained
his degree of Doctor of Law. For the past 5 years he has been
employed with the "Hearst Publishing Corporation," and in
connection with his work has been travelling extensively. Prior
to his coming to the Far East he was in Italy on his long leave,
but before the expiration of his leave received instructions to
proceed to the Far East on an urgent mission. He intends to
publish two books in America entitled "Around the World" and
"Reminiscences" respectively. Further he stated that he knew 14
languages including old Greek and Latin, that his mother
resided in Nice, France, and that his brother was in Abyssinia,
where he managed their plantations.

It is reported that his brother Alexander Vladimirovitch
Tatischeff and his brother-in-law named Hvostoff, who reside in
Addis Abeba, Abyssinia, were on friendly terms with a represent-
ative of the Soviet Trade Mission who visited that country in
1934, and that they established in Addis Abeba a firm to deal
in Soviet goods. In connection with this they were ostracized
by the majority of the Russian community in Addis Abeba.

1935年2月20日，当地俄文报纸刊登了对塔季谢夫伯爵的采访。从这些采访中可以看出，他的父亲曾是莫斯科联合银行（Union Bank）主席，俄国革命爆发后离开该国前往阿比西尼亚（即埃塞俄比亚），并随后在那里去世。塔季谢夫15岁时加入“白军”。他在俄国内战期间服役，并晋升为中尉。因受重伤，他乘坐一艘英国船只撤离到君士坦丁堡。后来他居住在马耳他，随后在英国，在牛津大学学习法律并获得法学博士学位。过去5年，他受雇于“赫斯特出版公司”（Hearst Publishing Corporation），并因工作关系广泛旅行。在来到远东之前，他正在意大利休长假，但在假期结束前接到指示，因紧急任务前往远东。他打算在美国出版两本书，分别题为《环游世界》和《回忆录》。此外，他还声称自己通晓14种语言，包括古希腊语和拉丁语，母亲居住在法国尼斯，兄弟在阿比西尼亚，负责管理他们的种植园。

据报道，居住在阿比西尼亚亚的斯亚贝巴的他的兄弟亚历山大·弗拉基米罗维奇·塔季谢夫（Alexander Vladimirovitch Tatischeff）和名为Hvostoff的妹夫，与1934年访问该国的苏联贸易代表团代表关系友好，并在亚的斯亚贝巴成立了一家经营苏联商品的公司。因此，他们被亚的斯亚贝巴的大多数俄国社区所排斥。

Tatischeff receives his correspondence c/o the American
Express Co., No. 110 Kiangse Road. During the latter part of
February, a foreigner called at the offices of that company
to make enquiries regarding Tatischeff who, he stated, intended
to buy from his firm goods to the total value of several
thousand dollars and gave as reference the American Express Co.
The visitor was informed that Tatischeff had no banking account
with the American Express Co., nor otherwise known there, except
for the fact that he was receiving his correspondence c/o the
company. Towards the end of February, Tatischeff visited
the Alexander Clark Co., Ltd., No. 1 Nanking Road, and selected
two articles to the total value of $2,000. He then stated
that he would call again to make his final choice and mentioned
as reference the American Express Co. Since that time he
did not visit this firm.

Soon after his arrival in Shanghai Tatischeff made the
acquaintance of a Russian named P.E. Zelenkoff, and his daughter,
Miss Zelenkoff, an employee of the "Salon Bella", No. 1117
Avenue Joffre. After a week's time he asked Miss Zelenkoff
to marry him. She agreed to do so, despite the opposition
on the part of her father, who asked Tatischeff to leave his
daughter alone. In connection with his alleged engagement
with Miss Zelenkoff, Tatischeff made arrangements for a party
of 30 persons at the Leinemann's German Cafe, No. 870 Bubbling
Well Road. When asked for a deposit, Tatischeff left and has
not since visited the Cafe in question.

A few days ago he visited the Robert Dollar Co., No. 51
Canton Road and stating that he intended to proceed to America
asked to reserve for him a "cabine de luxe" in the s.s. "President

塔季谢夫（Tatischeff）的信件由江西路110号美国运通公司（American Express Co.）代收。二月下旬，一名外国人前往该公司办公室，查询有关塔季谢夫的情况，称此人打算向其公司购买总值数千美元的商品，并以美国运通公司作为资信证明。来访者被告知，塔季谢夫在美国运通公司既无银行账户，也非该公司所熟知的客户，仅知其信件由该公司代收。二月底，塔季谢夫前往南京路1号的亚历山大·克拉克有限公司（Alexander Clark Co., Ltd.），挑选了两件总价值为2,000美元的商品。随后他表示将再次前来做出最终选择，并提及以美国运通公司作为资信证明。自那以后，他未再光顾该商行。

塔季谢夫抵达上海后不久，结识了一位名叫P.E.泽连科夫（P.E. Zelenkoff）的俄国人及其女儿泽连科夫小姐（Miss Zelenkoff），后者是霞飞路1117号“贝拉沙龙”（Salon Bella）的雇员。一周后，他向泽连科夫小姐求婚。尽管其父反对并要求塔季谢夫不要纠缠其女，她仍同意了婚事。就其与泽连科夫小姐所谓的婚约而言，塔季谢夫在静安寺路870号的莱内曼德式咖啡馆（Leinemann's German Cafe）安排了一场30人的聚会。当被要求支付定金时，塔季谢夫离去，此后再未光顾该咖啡馆。

几天前，他前往广东路51号的罗伯特·多尔公司（Robert Dollar Co.），声称打算前往美国，要求为其预订将于4月13日驶离上海的“林肯总统号”（s.s. "President Lincoln"）轮船的一间“豪华舱”（cabine de luxe），但未支付任何定金。

So far no complaints have been made to the Police
against Tatischeff. Persons who have been in contact with
him while in Shanghai describe him as a pathological liar.
However, it would seem to appear from the above that his movements
are worth watching.
Tatischeff resided at No. 477 Rue Auguste Boppe
until February 14 when he removed to an unknown address.
Leo Berg referred to above claims to be a Swedish
citizen, who was born in 1889 at Upsala. He travels on
Swedish passport No. 459 issued on 3.5.34 at Stockholm which
bears a Chinese visa issued in Berlin on 15.1.35. He gave
his home address as No. 24 Luterstrasse, Berlin, and stated
that he would stay in China for one month. When asked by
the boarding house-keeper to produce his passport for registra-
tion Berg replied that it was in the Swedish Consulate. On
the same day he absconded without paying his bill. He appears
to be a Russian of Caucasian origin and a person of a very
limited education.
Mrs. Maria Vladimirovna Danish, 33, another companion
of Tatischeff, is a Russian emigrant, and is in possession of
passport No. 226132 issued by the local Public Safety Bureau
on October 4, 1934. She is reported to be Berg's paramour,
and seems to be in possession of considerable funds. As
reference she mentioned one Mrs. Kornetzky, 484 Rue Cardinal
Mercier.
Photograph of Count V.V. Tatischeff is attached
herewith.
D. C. (Special Branch).
Jitcheremshansky

迄今为止，警方尚未收到针对塔季谢夫的投诉。在上海与他有过接触的人形容他是一个病态的说谎者。然而，从上述情况看来，他的行踪似乎值得监视。
塔季谢夫一直居住在奥古斯特·博佩路（Rue Auguste Boppe）477号，直至2月14日搬往一个不详的地址。
上文提到的利奥·伯格（Leo Berg）自称是瑞典公民，1889年出生于乌普萨拉（Upsala）。他持有1934年5月3日在斯德哥尔摩签发的第459号瑞典护照，该护照上有1935年1月15日在柏林签发的中国签证。他提供的家庭住址是柏林卢特大街（Luterstrasse）24号，并称将在华停留一个月。当寄宿公寓管理员要求其出示护照以便登记时，伯格回答说护照在瑞典领事馆。同日，他未付账单便潜逃。他似乎是高加索裔俄国人，受教育程度很低。
玛丽亚·弗拉基米罗芙娜·达尼什（Maria Vladimirovna Danish）夫人，33岁，塔季谢夫的另一位伴侣，是一名俄国流亡者，持有1934年10月4日由本地公安局签发的第226132号护照。据报她是伯格的情妇，似乎拥有相当多的资金。她提到的资信证明人是梅神父路（Rue Cardinal Mercier）484号的科尔内茨基（Kornetzky）夫人。
随函附上V.V.塔季谢夫伯爵的照片。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date February 19, 1935.

Subject (in full) Arrival in Shanghai of Count Tatisheff self described
representative of the New York Herald.

Made by D.S.I. Golder. Forwarded by 〔此处转录不清〕

Count Tatisheff, a member of the former Russian
nobility and previously domiciled in Italy, arrived in Shanghai
from Naples on the s.s. Haruna Maru on February 19, 1935.
Enquiries regarding him indicate that he will attempt
to interest the Chinese in the purchase of Italian arms; so
much he admitted to one of his fellow passengers. When landing,
however, he described himself as a journalist and a representative
of the New York Herald. It is believed that he intends putting
up with Mrs. A.S. Zaitzeff who operates a boarding house at
No. 477 Rue Auguste Hoppe, French Concession.
In conversation with a member of the S.M.P. he stated
that he intended staying here some time and hoped eventually
to proceed to America, of which country he is anxious to
become a citizen.
D.S. Tcheremshansky assisted in this enquiry.

D.S. Tcheremshansky. Em Golder
D.S.B. 19/2. D. S. I.

work in which he was engaged

事由（全称） 自称为《纽约先驱报》代表的塔季谢夫伯爵抵沪。

制作人 D.S.I. 戈尔德（Golder）。 转呈人 〔此处转录不清〕

塔季谢夫伯爵，前俄国贵族成员，此前寓居意大利，于1935年2月19日乘坐“榛名丸”号（s.s. Haruna Maru）从那不勒斯抵达上海。
对他的调查显示，他将试图引起中方对购买意大利武器的兴趣；他对一名同船乘客承认了这一点。然而，在登陆时，他自称是记者及《纽约先驱报》的代表。据信，他打算住在法租界奥古斯特·霍佩路（Rue Auguste Hoppe）477号经营寄宿公寓的A.S.扎伊采夫（A.S. Zaitzeff）夫人处。
在与一名工部局警务处人员交谈时，他表示打算在此停留一段时间，并希望最终前往美国，他迫切希望成为该国公民。
D.S. 切列姆尚斯基（Tcheremshansky）协助了此次调查。

D.S. 切列姆尚斯基。 Em 戈尔德
D.S.B. 19/2. D. S. I.

D. C. （特科）。 S2，是否了解他在欧洲从事的工作。
